records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — The dialog redefines guest-list validation instead of sharing the API schema, so client and server rules can drift.
records.rationale: The finding is factually accurate: AddGuestsDialog.tsx defines a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema (z.array(z.string().email()) plus a uniqueness refine) while the server has its own ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts (z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine). The drift is already real: the client enforces uniqueness, the server does not, so duplicated guests could pass API validation. This is a concrete, decision-relevant maintainability/consistency concern for a maintainer reviewing this new endpoint, not a mere style nit.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — A calendar update failure is surfaced after the attendee rows have already been committed, leaving booking state out of sync with the calendar.
records.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking attendees are created via prisma.booking.update (committed) before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails but guest rows remain committed, so booking state and the external calendar are out of sync with no rollback or compensation — exactly the mechanism the finding describes. Only the email send is wrapped in try/catch; the calendar call is not.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — The attendee rows commit before the external calendar update, so an update failure returns an error after guests were persisted and retries can cascade into duplicate additions.
records.rationale: The diff shows prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany committing the new guests (addGuests.handler.ts) followed by `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with no transaction or catch around it. If the calendar update throws, the mutation errors out after guests were already persisted, leaving DB/calendar state inconsistent; on retry the uniqueGuests filter (which excludes emails already in booking.attendees) yields an empty array, triggering the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST error, so the user cannot recover. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167 — Email delivery failures are swallowed and the mutation reports success, leaving affected attendees without notification and no retry path.
records.rationale: The diff shows `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` — the error is swallowed, no error surfaced to user or logs beyond console.log, and the handler returns success, so attendees may never be notified with no retry path. This is verifiable in the diff; whether it's a defect or deliberate fire-and-forget design is debatable, but the mechanism described is accurate. It's arguably intentional (emails are best-effort), so confidence moderate.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Email delivery failures are swallowed and the mutation still reports success, silently leaving calendar participants without the announced update.
records.rationale: The diff at addGuests.handler.ts lines ~168-172 shows `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` followed by `return { message: "Guests added" }` — email failures are swallowed (only console.log) and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows 'guests_added' toast even when notification emails failed. The mechanism described is verifiable in the diff; whether this rises to a defect vs. deliberate fire-and-forget design is debatable, but the silent failure path is real.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Existing-attendee and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive, allowing casing variants to bypass blacklist policy and add duplicate logical recipients.
records.rationale: The diff lowercases blacklist entries (`process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but then compares `blacklistedGuests.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so a guest like `Bad@Example.com` bypasses the blacklist. Similarly, the existing-attendee dedup uses exact `guest === attendee.email`, so `User@Example.com` vs `user@example.com` would be added again, creating a duplicate logical recipient. Both comparisons are visible verbatim in addGuests.handler.ts.

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Guest rows are committed before the calendar update, so a calendar-provider failure leaves guests persisted but impossible to retry through this endpoint.
records.rationale: The diff shows the handler first commits new attendees via prisma.booking.update (createMany of guestsFullDetails), then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If the calendar update throws, the TRPC mutation fails but the guests remain persisted. Worse, on retry the uniqueGuests filter removes any guest already in booking.attendees, so a retried request would hit `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, making recovery through this endpoint impossible. This is a verifiable, real defect introduced

records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The server accepts duplicate guest emails, so a crafted request bypasses the client-only uniqueness check and can create duplicate attendees or fail the whole batch.
records.rationale: The server schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refinement, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only removes emails matching existing attendees (`booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`) or the blacklist — duplicates within the submitted guests array are not filtered and would be created via createMany. The uniqueness check exists only client-side (ZAddGuestsInputSchema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx), so a direct API call bypasses it, exactly as the finding describes.
